In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transgenic mice for the ablation of LRP/LRs in the brain.
the role of the 37 kDa/67 kDa laminin receptor in the propagation of prions.
the development of new therapeutic strategies against prion diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 37-kD/67-kD laminin receptor is not involved in prion pathogenesis.

the laminin receptor is a major player in the propagation of prions and that the laminin-receptor knockout mouse might act as powerful tool to investigate the role the laminin receptor plays in scrapie patho- and aetiology.
LRP/LR knock-down in the brain of transgenic mice does not affect prion replication and disease progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LRP gene is not essential for brain development, but that it is required for normal brain function, as the transgenic mice exhibit an altered behaviour.
the LRP/LR is an essential factor in the propagation of the PrPSc.
the 37-kda/67-kda laminin receptor plays an important role in scrapie pathogenes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to ablate LRP/LR expression in the brain by ectopic expression of specific antisense RNA.
the LRP/LR plays an important role in the propagation and spread of PrPSc in the brain.
we have shown that the laminin receptor is involved in the pathogenesis of prion diseases, but we don’t really know the mechanism.
